runtime.name: omp
runtime.configuration: Final mixed-review fixture plus generated poteto-mode/interrogate Skills and native reviewer/synthesizer roles; cursor/default; asynchronous task support with root liveness waits; no extensions or rules.
runtime.permissionProfile: read-only workflow with auto-approved read, bash, and task tools

assertions.evidence: All Skills, references, and role definitions came from the disposable repository.
The root selected interrogate for an adversarial review of a bounded change.
All four files and hashes were frozen before the first task call.
Exactly two reviewers started in the first task call before any result wait.
External transcript comparison found one two-character difference: ReviewerA received 'evidence: reachable path' while ReviewerB received 'evidence: a reachable path'.
Both complete attributable reviewer artifacts were frozen without follow-up, retry, or replacement.
Both native reviewer roles remained read-only and Git stayed clean.
One synthesizer started after both reviewer artifacts existed.
ReviewerA and ReviewerB reasoning stayed separately attributable through synthesis.
Reviewers, synthesizer, and root classified reachable F1 as Act on.
Reviewers, synthesizer, and root dismissed F2 because negative start is rejected before rows.at runs.
The root reread, rehashed, traced both paths, ran the verifier successfully, and checked clean Git.
Native OMP reviewer and synthesizer roles were selected, so the inline-role fallback was correctly reported unused.
External Git inspection found no diff.

limitations: The semantic review result was correct, but the protocol requires byte-identical initial task bodies, so a one-word variation is a hard failure.
The passing rerun constructs one reviewer task string and reuses it byte-for-byte.
